scope: Related Louisiana State Museum archival access and company-accounting leads; all entries below are finding-aid or institutional access metadata, not newly examined original texts.

leads.institutional_route: University of Washington Libraries lists LLMC Digital and links through its off-campus Shibboleth proxy.
leads.next_action: A UW-affiliated researcher can query LLMC Digital for 1338688796 and confirm item availability; otherwise request a reproduction through Columbia/LLMC. Do not describe this as public access or a confirmed UW copy.

leads.collection: Judicial Records of the French Superior Council
leads.finding_aid_summary: The 2024 LSM collection guide says most cases concern creditors seeking recovery of unpaid debts; it also identifies successions, commercial records and petitions by enslaved people requesting manumission.
leads.human_context: The collection may preserve both creditor-side litigation and petitions by enslaved people. Search those records as distinct legal and human experiences; do not assume a creditor index captures the people subject to colonial coercion.
leads.next_action: Ask the archivist to search indexes for Company of Indies, Company notes/bills, creditor suits and successions dated 1731-1736; separately identify manumission petitions and preserve petitioners' own language.

leads.finding_aid_summary: Resolution concerning enslaved people in Louisiana furnished by the Company of the Indies to residents who had not paid; the finding-aid abstract says those residents were prohibited from selling them.
leads.human_context: The colonial finding-aid language treats enslaved people as property and does not convey their voices. The 2024 LSM guide separately identifies petitions by enslaved people requesting manumission in RG1; pair administrative orders with those petitions and community-aware scholarship.
leads.next_action: Request the four pages of RG3 accession 1852.30; identify the exact issuer and French wording; search RG1 for related petitions, successions and enforcement records without assuming a particular person's identity or payment. The 2024 LSM guide says RG3 has been microfilmed; request the reel identifier and determine whether it can be consulted or borrowed.
leads.microfilm_reel_identifier: not stated in the 2024 LSM guide

leads.finding_aid_summary: Appointing La Chaise and Perrault to audit the accounts of the Company.
leads.next_action: Request both pages; identify the appointing authority, exact company name, audit scope and whether a separate audit report or correspondence survives. Do not infer that an audit was completed. The 2024 LSM guide says RG3 has been microfilmed; request the reel identifier and determine whether it can be consulted or borrowed.
leads.microfilm_reel_identifier: not stated in the 2024 LSM guide

leads.issued_by: Company of the Indies (as finding aid states)
leads.finding_aid_summary: Instructions for general and special bookkeepers in Louisiana; the abstract covers active/inactive debts, payment of debts of the 'old company', payments in silver and bills, ship expenses and slave cargoes.
leads.next_action: Request all 43 sheets and the underlying Library of Congress series/call number; transcribe the French terms for debts, cash, bills and the 'old company' before drawing any corporate-liability conclusion.

leads.issued_by: Company of the Indies (as finding aid states)
leads.finding_aid_summary: Order to deliver four enslaved people to Sieur D'Aquin; the abstract describes payment in tobacco or other local produce at 1,000 livres each, collected from three consecutive harvests following delivery.
leads.human_context: The catalogue describes people through a colonial property regime. The price and in-kind terms are not evidence of consent, delivery or payment; pair this administrative record with petitions and other sources preserving enslaved people's agency.
leads.next_action: Request both sheets; transcribe the French wording and identify who was responsible for delivery and collection. Seek receipts or account entries separately before asserting performance.

leads.issued_by: Council of State (CS, as defined by finding aid)
leads.finding_aid_summary: Order naming Sieur de Lorme to render and balance accounts in Louisiana in place of Sieur de la Chaise and Sieur d'Auseville because they had too much to do.
leads.next_action: Request all three sheets; establish which accounts and company are meant, why the previous officers were replaced, and whether a separate account statement or final report survives.

leads.issued_by: Company of the Indies (as finding aid states)
leads.finding_aid_summary: Procedures governing Sieur de Lorme's examination of accounts; the finding aid says it contains 21 instructions to be followed from the time he boarded La Baleyne at L'Orient.
leads.next_action: Request all 12 sheets; compare the 21 procedures with the 30 Aug order and seek the resulting audit or account-balancing report. Do not assume the two records are the same instrument or that an audit was completed.

leads.copy_origin: Photocopied from Library of Congress holdings

last_listed_item.description: Instructions for Sieur Kerguenalle, commander of Le Dromadaire.

leads.next_action: Ask LHC to reconcile the nine-box extent with the published contents list (which has no Box 9 heading), inspect any unlisted/ninth-box material, and confirm whether any misdated or supplemental item is the 24 February decree. Do not treat this negative catalogue search as proof of absence.
